comedian: moose unmoved on the far shore, returns holding a number

treatment.judge_reasoning: All four pitches converged on the take-a-number ticket, which carries the angle (order, not whether) in one object any Alaskan has stood in line for. The dramatist's shore dispenser and loop back to an empty queue gives the cleanest bookend. The explainer's dot field is the hardest-landing number drawn physical. The comedian's gags stay off the whales and the named people. The enthusiast supplies the fair upside so the Test scene reads as a case and not a strawman.

palette.sky: #3A3354 true violet blue hour, rising to #54506E at a pale horizon band
palette.test_light: #EEE27A acid lemon, hue near 57 degrees, lit by a lamp cone and window, paper pure white with slate ink inside it
palette.mood: cold blue hour, one acid lemon lamp for the applicant best case, back to blue hour
palette.divergence: 11-09 oxblood and walnut, 11-08 permafrost, 11-07 transformer teal, 11-06 tangerine office, 11-02 midnight indigo cab with sodium amber. This film moves the sky off 11-02 indigo to a true violet and never uses amber: its warm moment is a pale lemon daylight, its hero is a vermilion machine on slate shingle, and the cream paper is the only recurring neutral. No teal desk, no oxblood. Revised 2026-11-10: sky moved off 11-02 indigo to slate violet, vermilion belongs to the machine and ticket only, stamps are ink slate or cream, never red.

shape_language: Rectilinear, perforated and stamped paper against round organic water and animal shapes. The machine is a fat vertical box, the whales are soft ovals, proposed hardware is dashed ghost outlines. The contrast is bureaucracy against tide. There is always one curve in a frame of rectangles: tide behind the counter glass, a tide clock beside the wall clock, the inlet through the spruce at the mailbox, a water curve on the pegboard, the window onto water in the lemon room. The cable on the chart follows a curved tidal contour and the 331 block at the table edge has a soft water edge.

casting.reasons: The shelf covers every actor. The machine is the one gap, a reusable prop that can serve future permit and queue stories. Heroes of the last two films (StampBot, Reels, Strand) are not used.
casting.machine_sign: The shore machine sign carries queue states only: P-15423 at the open, NOT YET at shot 13, NEXT at the moose. The deadline has its own small docket sign that flips to CLOSED over the window at the shutter drop.

motion_language: The dispenser clacks and shudders with squash and overshoot on every ticket. Paper entrances anticipate, overshoot and settle. The dot field drains with eased cohorts. Held figures use IdleFigure cues, held props use HeldProp and HeldTravel.

composition.focal_hierarchy: each shot names one 55 to 70 percent hero, a 20 to 30 percent support and 10 to 15 percent world
composition.negative_space: the empty queue rope at the open and the close, held as the quiet beat
composition.safe_area: hero and plates within y 420 to 1500 of the 9:16 master, sky and water above and shingle below stage the vertical
composition.signature_shot: the 1979 field of 1,300 white dots draining down to a 331 block while the NOT THE SAME 1,300 stamp parts them from the fleet's permit tags
composition.stamp_cap: Two stamps only, PRELIMINARY PERMIT and NOT THE SAME. Everything else is native to the ticket: perforation tears, bare unpinned pegs, a rubber band, a pencil. Stamp ink is slate on the cream body of the ticket (the vermilion band is only its header) and on cream paper, never red.
composition.declined_note: Critic note declined with measurement: the closing shore is not emptied of people because the VO names the borough, fleet and NOAA at that moment and the three silhouettes stop at the rope without sitting, so the question stays a question.
